severity_policy.p3_rule: Only retain a P3 candidate when a concrete exploit path, security boundary violation, reproducible proof and Wise-specific impact are already demonstrated. Do not spend scheduled runs on generic P3 discovery.
severity_policy.promotion_rule: Scanner output, code smell, dependency CVE, theoretical impact or configuration hardening does not establish severity.

A.name: CI/CD and repository trust
A.focus: GitHub Actions trust boundaries, fork/PR execution, token permissions, release/signing/package publication and repository takeover paths

B.name: Authentication, authorization and signing
B.focus: Wise-owned authn/authz, OAuth/session/token/signature/idempotency/cryptographic enforcement and privilege-boundary failures

C.name: Code execution and unsafe data flow
C.focus: Attacker-controlled input reaching command execution, deserialization, template/build execution, parser boundary or injection with concrete high-impact consequences

D.name: Infrastructure and deployment integrity
D.focus: Wise-specific IaC, cloud/deployment trust, artifact configuration, secret exposure paths and privilege escalation proven safely without touching live infrastructure

E.name: Cross-repository and supply-chain integrity
E.focus: Wise-specific dependency, build, release, package, artifact and cross-repository trust failures; third-party-only bugs are rejected

evidence_gates.G0: Exact in-scope repository and attacker-controlled entry point
evidence_gates.G1: Exact commit, shipped/relevant code path and trust boundary
evidence_gates.G2: Reproducible non-destructive proof with honest/negative control
evidence_gates.G3: Independent security invariant and concrete Wise-specific impact
evidence_gates.G4: Priority justified as P0/P1/P2 or exceptional P3, duplicate-reviewed, sanitized reproduction ready

notes: Any public repository directly under the transferwise GitHub organization is in GitHub scope except transferwise/pipelinewise.
Repositories outside transferwise are rejected before checkout.
A vulnerability inherited from a third-party library/project is not treated as rewardable without Wise-specific vulnerable behavior or integration.
Sample/placeholder secrets in documentation, examples, tests, fixtures, and CI are suppressed when clearly non-production.
Credential candidates are never validated by automation against Wise systems.
Static/scanner output is only a lead. A reportable finding requires repository/commit/path evidence, reproducible proof, demonstrated impact, priority justification and duplicate review.
Five issues are known to have been reported, but fingerprints are not available in this policy snapshot; every candidate therefore retains a manual duplicate-review requirement.
Scheduled lanes target P0-P2. P3 is retained only when the exploit and concrete impact are already strong enough to justify continued work; general P4/P5 hunting is prohibited.
